hook: SCP-5733 is a 1983 slasher movie on VHS that nobody has any other record of. At minute 97 the final girl, Heather, hides in the basement, turns to the camera and begs whoever is watching to help her survive. The rest of the file is a run of test logs, each one a different expert trying to coach her out alive, so read it like a series of short horror episodes.
whyItMatters:
It takes the habit of yelling advice at a horror movie and makes it literal. Every log follows the same rhythm, a clever plan, a moment of hope, then the killer one step ahead and a cut to black, and the fun is in how each new idea gets countered.

It also plays fair with genre logic. The killer seems to know the viewer's advice in advance, which turns the tests into a duel between the audience and the film itself.
thingsToNotice:
Watch the counters escalate to match the advisers. The unloaded shotgun, the slashed tires, the corpse in the neighbor's bed and the blood note reading "The only Foundation here is FEAR" all answer advice before it lands, and when Heather learns hand-to-hand combat or thaumaturgy, the killer suddenly fights just as well or casts spells of its own. The footnote about the clocks saying morning while the light says midnight is a small sign that her world doesn't run on real rules.

Dr. Carpenter's final test removes himself from the decisions by drawing instructions at random from bowls, and it works until the road out simply loops through darkness back to the cul-de-sac. With the last card he already knows the answer, the killer dodges, and the torn sack shows Carpenter's own face. The file closes on a data-leak investigation and a single line saying another tape has turned up.
